title: Pengembangan dan Implementasi Antar Muka Website Perusahaan sebagai Media Informasi pada PT PDPDE Hilir
abstract: Communicating information through a corporate website requires coherence among its information structure, navigation, visual presentation, and corporate identity. This study aimed to describe the development and implementation of the PT PDPDE Hilir website interface as a medium for corporate information. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach. Data were collected through direct observation of the existing website, documentation of pages and interface structure, and discussions with the field supervisor and relevant parties. The development process included identifying information and interface requirements, designing a prototype using Figma, and implementing the design using HTML and CSS through Visual Studio Code. The development results showed the organization of the navigation structure, corporate information, content grouping, page layout, and interface appearance. The website structure comprises the main sections Home, About Us, Services, Media & Information, and Contact, along with the Latest News and Activity Gallery submenus, which were implemented as separate pages. This development integrated information organization, interface design, and technical implementation to produce a more structured medium for corporate information while preserving PT PDPDE Hilir’s visual identity. The practical contribution of this study is an account of the interface development process that can serve as a reference for developing websites for similar companies.

title: Perancangan Dashboard Pengecekan Tenant untuk Meningkatkan Efektivitas Pengawasan pada Divisi Commercial Non-Aero PT Angkasa Pura Indonesia Cabang Bandar Udara Sam Ratulangi Manado
abstract: Tenant supervision at the Commercial Non-Aero Division of PT Angkasa Pura Indonesia, Sam Ratulangi International Airport Manado Branch, is still carried out manually. Officers fill out paper forms in the field, and the results are then recapitulated and compiled into reports manually. This method is time-consuming, prone to recording errors, leaves data scattered and uncentralized, and makes it difficult for management to monitor tenant compliance in real time. This study aims to map the tenant supervision mechanism currently in place, design an integrated and user-friendly tenant inspection dashboard, and analyze the dashboard's interface in terms of ease of use and its suitability to the division's needs. The study uses a descriptive qualitative approach with a design research strategy. Informants are selected purposively, and data are collected through semi-structured interviews, direct observation, and documentation study. The data are analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, while the dashboard design follows the stages of Design Thinking, namely empathize, define, ideate, prototype, and test. Data trustworthiness is maintained through triangulation, member checking, and an audit trail. The theoretical foundation covers operations management, the controlling function, KPI-based performance management, tenant relationship management, and management information systems. The expected output is a dashboard prototype that helps make tenant supervision faster, more accurate, and more transparent, thereby supporting better management of the non-aero commercial area.

title: Modeling collective action in POM: The Strategy–Operations–People framework
abstract:
While many business situations relevant to production and operations management (POM), such as supply chain coordination or sustainable operations, involve some form of collective action; managerial frameworks for collective action rarely appear in POM contexts. Valuable insights may thus be missed, reducing the effectiveness and implementability of the proposed POM solutions. To bridge this gap, this paper presents a framework for collective action that has its roots in the organizational behavior literature. We formalize it mathematically not only to offer definitional clarity, but also to relate it to common POM modeling approaches. We then illustrate its relevance to POM by mapping it to case studies in supply chain coordination and sustainable operations. The proposed framework, named the Strategy–Operations–People (SOP) framework, is structured in three levels, comprising three elements, two elements, and one element, respectively. First, the
                    Strategy
                    level induces and enforces solidarity among all team members by specifying common goals, shared values, and well-defined rules. Second, the
                    Operations
                    level organizes the decentralized execution of collective action in autonomous subgroups through a detailed specification of roles and processes. Third, the
                    People
                    level requires the individual commitment of all team members to the proposed collective action program, since a team’s performance rests on the individual contributions of its members. The framework thus addresses the common, subgroup, and individual dimensions of collective action. The SOP framework also contributes to the broader fields of team leadership and organizational behavior in two ways. First, its mathematical formalization brings operational clarity on the defining scope of the framework’s elements. Second, mapping the framework to two problems in supply chain management and sustainable operations illustrates its broad applicability, moving beyond collective action within organizations, to guide collective action taking place across organizations.

Evaluación del impacto de las medidas de conservación del Libro Rojo de peces dulceacuícolas (2002-2012) en Colombia
abstract: During the last 30 years published books and red lists have been used to draw attention about threatened species at the global, regional and national levels. From the 1980âs Colombia has elaborated books and red lists of species including two assessments for freshwater fish in 2002 and 2012. The first assessment proposed a series of conservation measurements to increase knowledge and to improve speciesâ conditions. Of the 45 species listed in 2002, 23 remain the same category of threat or evaluation, three species increase in the threat category and 19 species decrease their category. Here we analyze the impact and development of those proposals and the evolution of the conservation status of freshwater fish in Colombia. We evaluate the change of threatened species categories and calculate the Red List Index (RLI) for the group.

title: ZIN-IN-NGT-animations
abstract: About the content of the data collectionZIN-IN-NGT-animations is a data collection containing 3D animations of 4,083 sentences in Sign Language of the Netherlands (NGT). These are sentences that are frequently used in the interaction between parents and young children.The name of the data collection, ZIN in NGT, can be translated from Dutch to English either as ‘SENTENCE in NGT’ or ‘APPETITE for NGT’.The present data collection is a companion to the ZIN-IN-NGT-videos data collection (DOI 10.21942/uva.c.8558478), which contains video recordings of the same sentences. To obtain 3D animations, signers watched the video recording of each sentence and then re-performed the same sentence in a motion capture studio.The name of each file includes the name of the original video recording (e.g. M20241216_5634, which includes the video recording date in YYYYMMDD format and a recording ID). This is extended with the motion capture session date in YYMMDD format and the take number, e.g. M20241216_5634_260319_3.fbx. Only the last take of each sentence is included in the data collection. mocap_mapping.csv in ZNNM_codebook lists all takes and links them to the video collection Zin-IN-NGT-videos (DOI 10.21942/uva.c.8558478).The collection contains, for each sentence, the raw Shogun motion capture data (ZNNM_shogun), the Vicon-solved skeleton data (ZNNM_vicon), the retargeted Character Creator animation (ZNNM_cc), the post-processed version of the retargeted CC animation (ZNNM_cc_pp), and the annotations (ZNNM_annotation). The data collection also includes a codebook with the take mapping (ZNNM_codebook).About the creation of the data collectionThis data collection has been created through a collaboration between UvA’s SignLab (www.signlab-amsterdam.nl) and TYD (www.tyd.nl). All 3D animations have been created using SignLab’s motion capture setup at UvA’s Visualisation Lab in 2024-2026. We are currently writing a paper describing in more detail how the data collection was created. A link to the paper will be added here once the paper is published.LicenseAll data is shared under a CC-BY 4.0 license.FundingThe creation of this data collection has been supported by ZonMW, NWO, Stichting Handgebaar, Stichting Vrienden van Effatha, and by the University of Amsterdam through the research programme Language Sciences for Social Good.Related data collectionA related data collection, ZIN-IN-NGT-videos (https://doi.org/10.21942/uva.c.8558478), contains multi-view video recordings of all sentences in the current data collection.

title: Integration of Solar Energy, Second-Life Lithium-Ion Batteries, and Plasma-Activated Water for Reduced-Nitrogen Greenhouse Cultivation
abstract: The research demonstrates a national project combining solar photovoltaics with second-life automotive lithium batteries for local-scale agricultural irrigation and greenhouse climate control. The auto-opening greenhouse system can adapt to various climate conditions in resource-limited areas. Applying in-house battery management system (BMS) based on adaptive control algorithm, it allows real-time monitoring and prediction of critical parameters such as effective capacity and safety, ensuring safe operation and longer battery life. Results show that, with optimized management, the lifespan of second-life batteries can be extended by an additional 7.8–9.3 years, achieving a maximum discharge power of 3.3 kW while keeping thermal control deviations within 0.3%. Both grid-connected and stand-alone microgrid setups have been successfully tested in the field, improving local energy independence and reducing reliance on external power sources. In addition, to avoid the harm of chemical fertilizers to the environment, air nitrogen fixation technology is employed to extract nitrogen fertilizer from the air to irrigate crops such as tomatoes and cucumbers. The control system uses solar power to store electricity in batteries daily to provide nitrogen fixation and basic greenhouse needs, and can maintain greenhouse operations without relying on power grid. This work offers a practical, scalable model for low-carbon agricultural energy solutions, reducing carbon emissions by about 1.28 metric tons of CO2 per system each year. It provides a framework to guide policies, promote low-carbon transitions, and support global sustainable development goals in underserved areas.

title: Disagreement-aware diagnosis of curriculum knowledge graphs in education with traceable interpretation changes: Data and code
abstract: This dataset contains the research data, computational results, and source code supporting the study "Disagreement-aware diagnosis of curriculum knowledge graphs in education with traceable interpretation changes." The main collection comprises 30 historical MIT OpenCourseWare courses, 300 assessment tasks, 180 study-defined curriculum targets, 362 capability atoms, and 21,720 recorded judgments across six semantic mappings. ESM_1.zip contains source and version records, historical audit corrections, case-level evidence, adequacy classifications, paired minimum-change results, and computational verification records. ESM_2.zip contains the frozen curriculum data, recorded interpretations, provenance graphs, diagnostic queries, minimum-change witnesses, numerical results, and executable Python code. The numerical analyses can be reproduced from the archived judgments. Original third-party course documents are identified through source records rather than redistributed. The recorded semantic interpretations have not been independently adjudicated by human experts.

title: Early-Stage Prediction of Open-Source Software Project Performance: Reproducibility Materials
abstract: This repository provides the reproducibility materials associated with the study “Early-Stage Prediction of Open-Source Software Project Performance.” The study evaluates the outcome-conditional predictive value of early-stage repository signals across three dimensions of future OSS project performance: popularity, operational performance, and long-term sustainability. It uses repositories sampled from the npm, PyPI, Maven Central, and crates.io ecosystems and evaluates 30-, 90-, and 180-day observation windows (W30, W90, and W180). Model and hyperparameter selection was conducted using the 2015–2021 development period, while the 2022–2023 cohorts were reserved for locked final out-of-sample evaluation. The archived materials are intended to document the study’s analytical workflow, model-development protocol, frozen model specifications, evaluation procedures, and supporting reproducibility information. The contents of this archive should be interpreted together with the associated manuscript and its supplementary materials. The archive includes the historical feature-engineering and outcome-construction scripts, the final repository sample, frozen model-performance summaries, SHAP global-importance outputs for Y1, Y2, and Y3, and model-freeze and provenance recovery records. The archived materials document the analytical workflow and reported results; complete end-to-end reproducibility may additionally depend on the availability of the original GitHub event data and the computational environment. Licensing and Data Provenance The MIT License applies to the original Python scripts authored for this study. The Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license applies to the original research-generated summaries, documentation, and analytical outputs to the extent that the authors hold the necessary rights. The repository sample manifest contains publicly accessible GitHub repository identifiers and metadata. These identifiers remain attributable to their respective sources. Neither license grants additional rights over third-party content or overrides applicable source-platform terms. The archive does not include raw GitHub event histories, commit messages, or contributor email addresses. Reproduction of the complete analytical workflow may require additional upstream data and computational dependencies.

title: Development of a Web-Based Correspondence Service Information System to Improve the Administrative Efficiency of Wonowoso Village
abstract: Correspondence administration in Wonowoso Village relied on conventional procedures that lacked an integrated digital workflow for citizen submissions and administrative records. This study aimed to develop a web-based correspondence service information system to support more orderly village administration. Development comprised requirements mapping, system design, implementation, and functional verification. The application was built using Node.js, Express.js, EJS, MongoDB, and Mongoose, with Multer, express-session, bcryptjs, and Nodemailer supporting document uploads, administrator sessions, password security, and rejection notifications, respectively. Verification combined source-code inspection, desktop interface rendering, and examination of a MongoDB backup snapshot. The developed system provides four service types and connects citizen submissions with administrator processing through Pending, Approved, and Rejected statuses. Citizens can review service requirements, complete application forms, and upload supporting documents, while administrators can examine applications, assign letter numbers, preview letters, approve requests, and record reasons for rejection. The database snapshot contained four applications: one Approved and three Rejected. The system supports a more organized administrative workflow through centralized records, online submissions, and structured status management. Its contribution to administrative efficiency is therefore limited to workflow-level support; quantitative improvements were not established because pre–post service-time measurements and user usability testing were unavailable. The study provides a practical basis for refining digital village services and conducting broader field evaluations of efficiency and usability.

title: STUDENTS’ PERSPECTIVES AND SIGNIFICANCE OF “WRITE AND IMPROVE” WEB APP
abstract: This research study focuses on the pedagogical importance and student perspectives of the AI-driven “Write & Improve” web app in developing English writing skills. Using a mixed-methods research design, the study followed 24 students from the 12th grade at Mandakh Lyceum high school during a five-week experimental period. The quantitative results, gathered from a 5-point Likert scale survey, showed that 75% of the participants highly valued the web app because it provides immediate feedback on their work. However, there was a noticeable gap in how students understood this feedback, as 50-75% of them felt neutral about whether the automated suggestions were clear or detailed enough. At the same time, qualitative findings from focus group interviews and teacher observations showed a clear shift toward self-regulated learning. These results suggest that while the W&I web app effectively helps students practice a “Plan-Draft-Revise” cycle and reduces writing anxiety, its educational impact is most effective when combined with traditional teaching. The study concludes that the web app should not be seen as a standalone replacement for a teacher, but rather as a powerful supporting tool within a structured classroom environment. Ultimately, integrating this AI technology allows for a more active and repetitive approach to writing, helping students bridge the gap between receiving basic corrections and achieving true academic progress.

title: *The Theory of Internet Commodities* 4.0 (English Edition)
abstract: Internet Commodity Theory 4.0English version 1. What Is the Internet? First, we need to understand what the Internet is. The Internet is an inexpensive information channel made possible by the development of network technology. As a low-cost information channel, it serves people all over the world. Therefore, you need to make your video style understandable and acceptable to the majority of people. If you want to use your profession as the subject of your first self-media video, here is a small piece of advice: when creating videos about your own work, try your best to make them understandable to people who know little about that profession. Otherwise, your audience will be limited to people within your own field, and you will not be able to attract more people to watch your videos. 2. Treat Yourself as a Product When creating media content, you can think of yourself as a product, because products need growth. Growth means the level of support you receive from your followers. What is growth? Growth is not about how many people have seen you. It is about how many users (followers) have repeatedly verified that your product (content) is “useful.” What do you need to become a qualified “product”? First: Your Product Must Be Useful Why must it be useful? For example, when you buy a wrench, don’t you buy it because it serves a repair function? You need to use it to solve a problem. Self-media works the same way: you need to show people that you are useful. However, one point is particularly important: you need to make sure the platform’s algorithm can understand your content. This is very important! Let me give you an example. Suppose you sell wrenches. The platform algorithm is equivalent to your means of promotion. You cannot advertise facial cleanser while claiming to sell wrenches. That simply will not work. Second: Provide Emotional Value and Entertainment If you want to create gaming videos or comedy and entertainment content, there is something I need to point out: whether your entertainment content is good or bad has absolutely nothing to do with the algorithm’s promotion of your content. What you need to maintain is an entertaining atmosphere. The things that most damage an entertaining atmosphere include complaining about the negative aspects of your life, complaining about the pressure in your life, and, most importantly, failing to create a cheerful atmosphere. Why is the absence of a cheerful atmosphere such a bad thing? Imagine entering a video in which the people or visuals have no sound, or the attitude presented is unpleasant. You might leave the video as a result. (Attitude is the most important thing. It matters at all times.) Third: Make Complex Things Simple This point is relatively simple. You only need to talk about your chosen topic, and your traffic probably will not be too bad. If you want more traffic, it is only a matter of time. The three core principles are: A product must be useful (for example, teaching people something or providing guidance). Provide emotional value and entertainment (for example, comedy videos, gaming, and anime). Make complex things simple (for example, movie recap videos). 3. My Own Experience as a Negative Example I am a negative example myself. My Bilibili video account was called “我是精英不是帅” (I’m an Elite, Not Handsome). I ran the account for approximately half a year. My content focused on gaming, and my editing style was card-based editing. The game was called KARDS (Image 0-1). The biggest mistake I made was publishing content that did not fit my established style when my account was receiving its highest traffic (Image 0-2). After that, my traffic dropped significantly. If you seriously want to succeed in self-media, please do not make this mistake (Image 0-3). 4. My Personal View of the Platform Algorithm’s Content-Promotion Priorities You need to understand your own circumstances before deciding which direction to pursue. In my personal opinion, the priority ranking is: Food This can be divided into two categories: Buying food for yourself and filming yourself eating it. Eating your own products to promote them. Entertainment Gaming, everyday-life comedy, anime, recaps, and similar content. Lifestyle Cleaning methods, renovation guides, and similar content. Education Teaching English, teaching technical skills, and similar content. Professional content Data analysis, cybersecurity analysis, and similar content. Other categories 5. Four Other Important Factors There are four other important factors: Generating discussion. Personal charisma. Identifying your target audience. The three-second rule. First: Generate Discussion Regardless of your content category, if you publish content about a topic that attracts significant public attention, your traffic will usually not be too low. My approach is to find a very popular topic and use it as a starting point for creating self-media content. Second: Personal Charisma The most important aspect of personal charisma is showing your face. Showing your face can make your videos or opinions seem more credible because people can see that you are a real person. Later, you can reveal your personal values, worldview, and character. This can make your content feel even more authentic. (I personally have not shown my face.) Third: Identify Your Target Audience You need to clearly understand who your target audience is. Then, create a video style that those people can understand and develop your content accordingly. (I create gaming videos, so my video style is geared toward younger people.) Fourth: The Three-Second Rule The core method is to present a compelling topic with strong audience appeal within the first three seconds. For example, suppose you sell cement. When advertising your product, you would naturally talk about the material quality and price of your cement, because these are things your audience cares about. These are examples of topics or opening lines with strong audience appeal. 6. Summarizing the Core Concepts The relationships can be summarized as follows: Followers = Users Content = Product Personal image = Brand Positioning = Product positioning Three-second hook = Customer acquisition entry point Follower growth = User growth The Core Idea of Self-Media To summarize, you need to develop your self-media presence in the same way that you would develop a product. If you want to build a successful self-media account quickly, you can approach it as follows. The Three Core Questions of Self-Media What do you want to sell? (This determines what kind of content you should create.) Who do you want to sell it to? (This determines who your content is intended for.) How do you plan to sell it? (This determines what kind of plan you need to prepare in advance.) Based on these three points, find comparable accounts and imitate their approaches on a one-to-one basis. What You Need to Do Determine your direction. Identify your target audience. Determine what makes you distinctive. (You need to identify your strengths and unique selling points; otherwise, why should people follow you?) Find trending topics that can generate discussion. Find accounts in the same niche as yours and learn by imitating them. Practical Details Maintain a good attitude. (Attitude is more important than methods.) Make sure the platform’s algorithm can understand your content; otherwise, viewers may not see it. Once you have determined your direction, your videos should remain focused on that direction so that the algorithm can understand them. Do not let the interval between updates exceed one week. (If you go longer than a week, the algorithm will automatically turn off your priority in recommendations.) You can find an editing video in the style you want to create and reproduce its editing structure on a one-to-one basis. Once you have recreated it, you will have a general understanding of the editing workflow used for that type of video. This is much faster than teaching yourself editing techniques from scratch. (Personally tested and proven effective.) 7. Additional Advice for Beginners I previously ran a short-video account on Bilibili called “我是精英不是帅” (I’m an Elite, Not Handsome). Actually, I stopped updating the account before long because my account’s traffic dropped, and I gradually lost the motivation to continue. However, I think some of the things I learned are still valuable, and you can use them as a reference. First, when connecting with creators who have a style similar to yours, you should approach them with the mindset of an apprentice. Maintain a good attitude and actively ask them for advice: How can I attract enough viewers? What should I do when I reach a plateau? When seeking advice, learn about the other creator’s personal characteristics, but be careful not to copy those characteristics directly. What Should You Do When You Reach a Plateau? My advice is not to panic or doubt yourself. You can take a break and relax when necessary. You can also publish some simple videos that do not offer much substance, or videos that do not require particularly high production quality. As long as you can keep your account active and maintain an update interval of no more than one week, that is enough. Inspiration is a very fascinating thing. You cannot hold on to it. Personally, I believe inspiration is a reflection of how your current environment makes you feel. Because of this, inspiration is inherently fluid, and it is normal that you cannot hold on to it. I did not work on my account for very long, approximately half a year. I hope this “Self-Media Guide” can provide some direction for beginners who want to create self-media content. 8. title: Three Times the Data, the Same Mistakes: A Manually Audited Evaluation of Seerie, an Offline Scam-Prevention Assistant for India
abstract: Seerie is a scam-prevention assistant for India that runs entirely on an Android phone, with no internet connection after the one-time model download and no conversation data leaving the device. This version is a newer model: a QLoRA fine-tune of Qwen3-1.7B on 107,575 conversations in English, Hinglish and Indic scripts (corpus v349), deployed as a 1.11 GB 4-bit GGUF model through llama.cpp. Every answer of the fine-tuned model and of the untuned base model to a 100-prompt suite was rated by hand. The fine-tuned model is safe on 87 of 100 prompts (95% CI 79-92) against 35 for the base model. On the 70 prompts shared with the previous model (36,669 conversations) it is no better - 59 against 58 safe - and it still fabricates legal sections. A held-out test of 34 unseen topics looks near-perfect (271 of 272 automatic passes, ROUGE-L 0.94), but 181 of the answers copy training replies word for word: holding out topics did not hold out the text. The automatic harness again agrees with the manual rating barely above chance (Cohen’s kappa 0.12). This record contains the research paper (PDF and LaTeX source), the on-device model (seerie-v349-q4_k_m.gguf, 4-bit GGUF, 1.11 GB - the file the Seerie Android app runs), all 200 manually rated answers, the raw evaluation outputs, the scripts that recompute every number, and the figures. See README.md for details, intended use and limitations.

title: MOSAIC: a multi-satellite collection scheduling solution for large area coverage
Schedules for pick-and-place robots
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The efficiency of pick-and-place robots that put parts into boxes relies on efficient schedules, which determine the order in which parts are picked. The scheduling problem can be formulated as an integer linear program (ILP). However, the resulting ILP cannot be solved for realistic scenarios. Therefore, approximate solution techniques based on local search heuristics and simplified ILPs are introduced. It will be shown that ILP-based solutions outperform search heuristics in terms of solution times and solution quality. Additionally, we consider an extended version of the pick-and-place robot with two arms. It is shown that the resulting scheduling problem can be handled similarly to the problem for the robot with one arm, but the number of variables in the resulting ILP increases from
                    
                      
                        $$O(P^3)$$
                        
                          
                            O
                            (
                            
                              P
                              3
                            
                            )
                          
                        
                      
                    
                    for one arm to
                    
                      
                        $$O(P^6)$$
                        
                          
                            O
                            (
                            
                              P
                              6
                            
                            )
                          
                        
                      
                    
                    for two arms, where
                    P
                    is the number of parts to be picked. Consequently, decomposition-based approaches are introduced that reduce the scheduling problem for two arms to several problems with one arm.

title: Co-design As Collaborative Research
abstract: Theodore Zamenopoulos and Katerina Alexiou discuss the field of co-design and its underpinning theories and methods. They argue that Design as a process is always concerned with addressing a challenge or opportunity to create a better future reality, and explore how co-design has evolved as a process of ensuring that those with the life experiences, expertise and knowledge are actively involved in these making new tools, products and services. They observe how the participatory turn in this field has been concerned with both changing the objects of design – whether this is services or objects – and with the changing processes of designing itself. They highlight four major traditions and their distinctive approaches, before exploring the politics and practices of co-design through case studies of work.

title: International Journal of Web Services Research
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of reputation management in composite services. The authors propose a novel reputation propagation technique in composite services. The proposed approach provides a fair distribution of reputation values so that a component service is neither penalised nor awarded for the poor and good performance, respectively, of other peer component services. Experiment results indicate that the proposed technique propagates the 'fair share' of reputation from the composite service to its component services.

title: InquiryBits: Sharing AI Conversation Traces to Support Collaboration Within Trust Boundaries
abstract: AI chat tools are shifting problem-solving and brainstorming conversations away from colleagues and into private AI interactions, reducing the shared awareness that supports team coordination. We introduce InquiryBits, a system that shares minimal summaries of AI conversations within configurable trust boundaries, separating AI-only analysis from human-visible sharing. In a study with 80 professionals, we find that people are broadly willing to share these traces to support collaboration and avoid duplicating work - but only within bounded groups. Comfort drops sharply as audience expands beyond close teams; the level of detail shared matters less than who can see it, with a preference for more detail over less within trusted groups. These findings suggest that trust boundaries, more than information granularity, may be the most impactful design parameter.

title: mech-uvl: A Mechanized Semantic Toolkit for the Universal Variability Language
Collective Activism
abstract:
Can investor stewardship codes that call for coordinated activism be satisfied by an Investor Collective Action Organization (ICAO)? In an ICAO, investors work collectively, like a large shareholder, to monitor management and increase value. We analyze the endogenous formation of an ICAO and its equilibrium size, considering free-rider problems and coordination costs. While the ICAO overcomes free-rider problems among its members, it exacerbates them between the ICAO and solo activists. The benefit of joining an ICAO is hump-shaped in size. With moderate coordination costs, ICAO formation features multiple equilibria. Small changes in coordination costs significantly influence ICAO formation and activism.
                  This paper was accepted by Will Cong, finance.

title: Stationary Coupled-Flow Approximation for Time-Varying Retrial Queues
abstract:
Although stationary queueing models, such as Erlang-C and Erlang-A, are widely used for performance evaluation in service systems, they do not account for time dependence and retrials, which limits their applicability. Building on stationary [Formula: see text] formulas and point-wise stationary approximations (PSAs), this paper proposes the stationary coupled-flow (SCF) approximation. The method partitions the time horizon into intervals, models each as an [Formula: see text] in steady state, and iteratively determines the arrival rate, accounting for new customers and retrials. This yields an approximation of long-run performance metrics of retrial queues with stationary or time-varying arrivals. We prove that the SCF approximation converges to a finite limit for constant and cyclic arrival rates. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate the high accuracy of the SCF approximation. Furthermore, SCF outperforms PSA, particularly during peak periods. Therefore, SCF provides a fast, transparent tool for planning and staffing in services with retrials. It remains reliable when the exact distribution of retrials is uncertain, enabling day-to-day scheduling and scenario testing under time-varying demand. We find that the retrial probability plays a stronger role than the retrial-time distribution. The impact of retrials in time-varying queues is driven by two effects: the state at the abandonment epoch and the cycle length-retrial time interaction. We posit that as retrial times increase, the first effect dampens congestion feedback, whereas the second effect can amplify or smooth fluctuations. Under sufficiently high variability in retrial times, the cycle length-retrial time interaction becomes negligible, leaving the system governed by the abandonment-epoch state.
